title: Warranty Failure Probabilities in Nevada Table
modelSelection: Select one or more flexsurvreg models (one per sub-period). With a single model and no cut-offs, behaviour is identical to before. With multiple models, enter the same cut-off production periods used in Build Nevada so each model is correctly matched to its cohorts.
subPeriodCutoffs: Cut-off production periods -- enter ONE per model in the SAME ORDER as the models appear in the selection box. Each cut-off is the FIRST production period of that model's own sub-period. With N models enter N cut-offs (e.g. 3 models need 3 cut-offs: 202011, 202111, 202311 means period 1 starts at 202011, period 2 starts at 202111, period 3 starts at 202311). The software sorts all (model, cut-off) pairs chronologically -- visual selection order does not matter. Leave blank when using a single model.
labelShipDataset: Step 2 - Select the shipment / delivery dataset (active dataset)
labelObsMonths: Step 3 - Specify the last observation / prediction period (i.e., how far out to predict)
obsProdMonthFmt: Last observation period format (ignored when entering a plain integer offset below)
lastObsMonth: Last observation period - enter either: (a) a CALENDAR date in the format selected above (e.g. 202806). The observation window runs from the first observable period up to this fixed end date -- older cohorts get more columns than newer ones (staircase Nevada shape). Works with both single and multiple models. OR (b) a PLAIN INTEGER (e.g. 30) meaning each cohort gets exactly that many observation periods from its own production date (every cohort gets the same number of columns). Works with both single and multiple models.
actualRepairCol: Select the column containing actual monthly repair counts. Rows with a numeric value = actual data already observed. Rows with NA = future period - those months use the forecast from the Nevada table. Leave empty to skip the Actual vs Forecast comparison and chart.
chkPrintProbTable: Print the full Failure Probabilities Nevada table in the output. Uncheck to suppress this (large) table and only show the summary, comparison table, and chart.
predictionBound: Prediction bound — controls which one-sided confidence bound of S(t) is used, at the confidence level the model was fit with (e.g. 95%). Estimated = point estimate (default). Lower bound of S(t) = pessimistic / worst case (more failures, because lower survival = higher failure probability). Upper bound of S(t) = optimistic / best case (fewer failures, because higher survival = lower failure probability).
newdatasetname: Output dataset name for the Nevada prediction matrix
labelDateNote: Select the format that matches EXACTLY how dates are stored. R make.names() changes (X prefix, dots) are handled automatically.

help.title: Failure Probabilities in Nevada Table
help.body:
Description

Produces the Failure Probabilities in Nevada Table matching other software's Warranty Analysis output. Each cell in the matrix shows the expected number of new repairs from that production cohort in that specific observation calendar month, based on the fitted parametric survival model.

Prerequisites
  1. Run Parametric Survival Analysis (Interval) to fit a flexsurvreg model. Save the model by noting its name (e.g. bsky_weibull_fit).
  2. Have a shipment dataset with production months and delivered counts available as the active dataset.
Observation months (auto-generated)
You only need to specify the last observation month. All column months from one month after the earliest production cohort up to the last observation month are generated automatically. The maximum age F(t) is also computed automatically as last_obs_month -' oldest_production_month.

Cell formula
Each cell = Delivered -- f(age_months)
where age_months = observation_month -' production_month (in months)
and f(t) = F(t) -' F(t-'1) is the incremental failure probability (expected proportion of units failing in that specific month of age).

Header rows
  • Cumulative Failure Probability - F(t) at ages 1..N
  • Failure Probability per month - f(t) = F(t) -' F(t-'1)
Column SUM row
The bottom row sums all cohort cells in each observation month, giving the total expected new repairs across all cohorts - the monthly warranty workload forecast.

Supported date formats
YYYYMM | MMM-YY | MMM-YYYY | YYYY-MM | MM/YYYY | POSIXct
